sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border E-Commerce Overseas Warehouse Order Fulfillment

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition) with EU-harmonised corporate, AML/CFT and tax rules; unitary national system with no sub-state tax differentiation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) - United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (1989)
BLEU - People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1986)
Luxembourg - United States Double Taxation Agreement (1996)
Luxembourg - China Double Taxation Agreement (1983, as amended by the 2014 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law); modified Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 July 2020 on AML/CFT procedure; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the SCSp; CSSF Regulation 12-02 as updated

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Incumbency/Good Standing of each non-EU corporate partner and of any foreign General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Companies Registry of the partner's country of domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) or Consular Legalization if the origin country is not a Hague Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised Power of Attorney from the General Partner and proposed managers to the Luxembourg incorporation notary and counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country of execution, authenticated through the applicable legalisation chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille when executed in a Convention state; alternatively signature-in-person before the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity documents (passport copies) and proof of residential address of the General Partner and underlying beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority / municipal administration of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies witnessed by the Luxembourg notary; documents notarised and apostilled if the person does not appear before the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English-to-French translation of the draft partnership agreement, UBO declaration forms and powers of attorney for registration annexure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator enrolled on the Luxembourg list of sworn translators (Ministry of Justice / VET)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No translation-specific consular legalization required for Luxembourg sworn translators; the notary certifies the translator's signature when the translation is annexed to the deed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the SCSp, its General Partner, limited partners holding at least 25% and all identified UBOs against (i) the Luxembourg CSSF consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List under Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and Regulation (EU) 833/2014; (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) the OFAC SDN List where USD clearing or payment rails are contemplated; and (v) domestic judicial and administrative files as applicable. PEP review covers senior foreign and domestic public-office holders, their family members and close associates under Article 3(2)-(7) of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, demanding enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification and senior-management approval. Customer due diligence documentation must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers - LBR single portal (https://www.lbr.lu), e-Etude module, integrated with the Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS) and the Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the working language of the RCS. The corporate name must be expressed in Latin script; French, German and English names are customary, but the statutory clause must contain 'Societe en Commandite Speciale' or its approved abbreviation 'SCSp' / 'S.C.Sp.' in French for registration purposes. Non-Latin (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) commercial trade names used in e-commerce operations require a fixed, officially consistent transliteration into Latin script which must match the RCS registration and bank account references exactly.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (requires CSSF banking licence)
Fonds / Fund / FCP / SICAV / SICAR / RAIF / UCI (requires CSSF prior authorisation or AIFM/UCITS regime)
Societe de Gestion / Asset Management / Wealth Management (regulated PSF/AIFM connotations)
Etat / Commune / Gouvernement / National / Royal (suggesting sovereign or state connection)
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross / Red Crescent (protected emblem)
Universite / Ecole / Lycee (unless accredited by the Ministry of Education)
Luxembourg / Letzebuerg / Luxemburg (requires demonstration of permitted official or municipal connection)
Societe Anonyme / S.A. / S.a r.l. (may be misleading for a partnership form)
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce (statutorily protected body)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A preliminary name clearance (certificat de non-confusion) is obtained via the notary through the LBR e-Etude portal and remains valid for 30 days. If the deed is not executed within that window, the name lapses and a fresh clearance must be obtained; no statutory right of extension exists. Upon rejection on grounds of identity, confusing similarity or a prohibited token, the RCS registrar issues a reasoned refusal (decision de refus). The applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (administrative chamber) within two months of notification, in accordance with Article 15 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002, after optional informal review by the Minister of Justice; expedited alternative is to amend the proposed name and file a new clearance on the same day.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. The SCSp must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg; a third-party corporate-services provider may register the SCSp at its premises only if it holds the relevant professional authorisation and provides actual administrative presence at that address. A mail-forwarding virtual office alone is not sufficient for an operational cross-border e-commerce fulfilment hub, which must additionally hold or lease a physical warehouse and local management substance in Luxembourg to support customs, VAT and employment substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk - moderate: approximately 20% annual probability of unannounced verification of the registered-office address by the RCS/LBR authorities, increasing to 35-50% probability for the operational cross-dock warehouse site through customs (ADA - Administration des Douanes et Accises), labour inspection (ITM) and Luxembourg VAT office visits during peak e-commerce cycles; unannounced AML/CFT inspections of the SCSp itself are unlikely absent a regulated-sector trigger.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance / certificat de non-confusion via LBR e-Etude
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per LBR fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of foreign partner documents (bundle of three originals)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the partner's country of origin and Consulate/Embassy of Luxembourg or BLEU consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention per-apostille fee (USD 20-60) plus consular tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of partnership agreement, powers of attorney and UBO declaration (English/Chinese to French, approx. 25 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg sworn translator registered with the Ministry of Justice (VET list)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 0.12-0.25 per word plus urgency uplift

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial incorporation deed and notary legal supervision for a standard SCSp with two partners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard SCSp deed (EUR 2,200-3,200 excluding VAT)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration of the SCSp and appointment of managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Societes via LBR
Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the incorporation deed in the RESA electronic compendium
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Official Journal / RESA publication service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office address service - initial setup fee (first year professional partner arrangement)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate services provider / registered agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC compliance advisory - UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening reports, source-of-funds review and due-diligence file certification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark hourly basis (EUR 350-450 per hour, 3-5 hours)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 81 to 93 (SCSp regime) introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of partnership (acte de société / partnership agreement) filed in electronic form through the e-RCS portal; notarial deed required only where contributions in kind are made
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital for an SCSp; capital contributions freely set by the partnership agreement. No escrow or capital deposit requirement; the managing partner must hold partnership funds at a Luxembourg credit institution and fulfil applicable AML declarations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the subscription of partnership interests in the Société en Commandite Spéciale is hereby approved, and the capital contributions, as recorded in the partnership agreement, are accepted from each founding limited partner. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the registered office of the society is adopted at the Luxembourg address stated in the articles, the commune and exact location having been disclosed to the Registrar. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the person named in the Partnership Agreement is appointed as Gérant, with full sole signatory power to represent the partnership before the Luxembourg Business Registers, the tax and registration administration, credit institutions and all public authorities, and is authorized to complete all formalities. This Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement and legal formalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (if capital in kind) or all partners and authorized counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the SCSp articles and partnership deed, obtain name availability through the Luxembourg Business Registers online portal, execute the deed by the general and limited partners, notarize only for in-kind contributions, and collect identification and compliance documents from all partners.
required_dossiers: Draft SCSp partnership agreement and limited partner schedule
Name availability confirmation issued by the Luxembourg Business Registers
Passport or national ID copies and proof of address of each partner
Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) register declaration form
Power of attorney for each represented founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS or notary objects to a term, amend the partnership agreement, re-execute the partners' resolution, and file a corrective instrument with the competent authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the corporate bank account and confirmation of contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the bank's corporate onboarding and AML/KYC forms, deposit the agreed partnership contributions, obtain the banker's confirmation of accounts opened in the SCSp name, and prepare the payment and source-of-funds documentation.
required_dossiers: Executed SCSp partnership agreement
AML/KYC questionnaire and source of wealth declarations
Passport copies and signatory authorization matrix
Bank reference or proof of address for relevant partners
Organizational chart and UBO declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond promptly to the bank's AML queries; where an institution declines, approach a qualified Luxembourg alternative bank or fintech with corporate account capability and resubmit the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: e-RCS platform of the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application through the secure e-RCS portal, pay the statutory registration fee, upload the executed partnership deed, and obtain the RCS registration number and NACE code allocation for warehousing and storage (NACE 52.10).
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp articles of association
RCS registration request form
Certified identification of the legal representative
Proof of name availability
Payment receipt of the official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query, file a corrective registration within the RCS rectification window, supplement the missing information, and pay any additional fee applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, transmit the required legal extract for electronic publication in the RESA official journal; confirm publication and download the certified publication reference for third-party use.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Consent of the appointed managing partner
Publication instruction form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published notice contains errors, request a rectifying filing from the RCS, obtain a revised RESA publication, and distribute the corrected extract to counterparties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and social security registrations (VAT, AEDT, CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration application for the warehousing and logistics activity, open the employer file with the CCSS, and register the operational management details for electronic filing and social declarations.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Proof of the Luxembourg registered office
Identity documents of the managing partner and signatories
Bank account confirmation
Warehouse location and activity description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT activation is delayed, follow up with AEDT via MyGuichet, correct any data inconsistencies, and request an activation status report or a direct liaison officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit (Autorisation d'établissement) for the operating warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes (DGCM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the establishment permit application through guichet.lu covering NACE 52.10 warehousing and storage; demonstrate professional reliability and, where required, the professional competence of the managing partner; obtain the permit and notify the registry.
required_dossiers: Autorisation d'établissement application form
Criminal record extract of the responsible person
Diploma or evidence of professional competence
SCSp partnership agreement
Warehouse lease contract and floor layout
Civil liability and property insurance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refusal may be administratively appealed to the Minister of the Economy within one month or challenged before the Administrative Tribunal; alternatively, remedy the missing competence evidence and reapply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes (DGCM)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the artisanal, commercial and industrial professions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency – Grand Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified facility (établissement classé) – Class 3 Declaration under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 March 2018 for non-hazardous warehousing and cross-dock storage; Class 2 Authorization required where covered floor area exceeds established thresholds or where refrigerant systems exceed F-gas charge limits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to municipal sewers must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 September 1993: pH 6.0–9.0, COD ≤ 1,000 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 600 mg/L, hydrocarbons ≤ 15 mg/L. Stormwater from loading docks must pass oil/grit separators before discharge; firewater retention capacity for racked storage must be sized to fire brigade specifications. VOC emissions remain minimal for storage-only activities, but diesel forklift and vehicle exhaust must meet workplace exposure limits; F-gas equipment, if installed, must be registered and maintained under Regulation (EU) No 517/2014.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) covering access roads, hydrant coverage, compartmentation and extinguishing systems; structural load inspection by an approved engineering bureau for pallet racking and mezzanine floors; occupational health and safety clearance by the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) under the Luxembourg Labour Code, including material handling equipment, vehicle routing, manual handling and employee health surveillance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes. Single digital portal: MyGuichet.lu operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the State IT Center (CTIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident SCSp without an establishment in Luxembourg, the general partner or authorized representative must (1) file the Luxembourg VAT registration application via the AED using Form 640 (or through MyGuichet.lu), providing the partnership deed, proof of identity of the general partner, and an appointment of a Luxembourg VAT representative if the SCSp has no fixed establishment in Luxembourg; (2) obtain a Luxembourg national business number (numéro national / matricule) and, where required, a taxpayer ID for direct tax purposes from the RCS / LBR; (3) request a dedicated VAT ID for the SCSp as a taxable person for VAT purposes, which is independent from the transparency status for income tax; and (4) update the registration upon any change in activity, turnover, or constitutional documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SCSp may elect, under Article 175 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR), to be treated as a transparent entity (default) or, upon application to the ACD, to be subject to corporate income tax / net wealth tax as a 'deemed corporate taxpayer'. Hybrid mismatch elections are limited; Luxembourg follows the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (ATAD) and the 2023 OECD hybrid mismatch rules, so the SCSp's fiscal transparency is respected unless a valid election to be taxable is made. For VAT, the SCSp may independently register as a taxable person even though it is transparent for income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No threshold for non-resident suppliers making supplies in Luxembourg; any taxable transaction triggers VAT registration. Domestic small business exemption: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (excluding VAT) applies only to established suppliers; cross-border and warehouse fulfillment activities are outside the small business exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or API stamping exists in Luxembourg for B2B invoices. E-invoicing is optional for B2B and mandatory only for B2G supplies to central government entities (PEPPOL / CIUS format). Luxembourg has committed to EU ViDA, so future e-invoicing and digital reporting mandates may apply from 2030. Until then, taxpayers must issue electronic invoices in any format and ensure full archiving and transmission to Luxembourg 'eCDF' where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (a) supplies of goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU (export) and (b) certain internationally linked services (e.g., transport and ancillary services directly connected to exports). For the cross-dock / overseas 3PL model, physical export from a Luxembourg warehouse to a non-EU buyer must be evidenced by export documentation. The exporter must hold this evidence within 90 days (or longer if justified) and must reflect the export in the periodic VAT return. Services physically performed outside the EU or directly related to exported goods qualify for zero-rating if the recipient is outside the EU or the effective use and enjoyment is outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A / Electronic Single Administrative Document)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill / CMR / rail consignment note)
Inward Remittance Certificate (evidence of payment received from the foreign buyer)
Proof of transport from Luxembourg to non-EU destination (carrier's certificate, GPS tracking, or customs stamped manifest)
Warehouse issuance / release order showing the goods left the bonded or VAT warehouse stock
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT authorities may disregard a claimed zero-rating if the export proof is incomplete, the goods did not physically leave the EU, or the payment is not received within the contractual terms. In such cases, VAT is clawed back at the standard rate (17%) from the supplier plus default interest from the end of the applicable VAT return period. Luxembourg provides a five-year limitation period for VAT assessments (ten years where fraud or under-declaration is established). Administrative fines for wrongful zero-rating range from EUR 250 to the total tax evaded, and criminal penalties up to double the tax due and/or imprisonment may apply where fraudulent intent is proven, under the Luxembourg General Tax Code (AO) and VAT law (Loi TVA).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Data (Confirmation annuelle des données)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) as operator of the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; must be filed within one calendar month following the anniversary of initial RCS registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice from RCS; court-ordered regularization; administrative/court fines up to EUR 5,000; persistent default may trigger judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Validation (Déclaration annuelle de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; annual validation due within one month of the anniversary of the original RBE declaration; amendments due within one month of any beneficial-ownership change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 4,000 and/or imprisonment up to 18 months for natural persons; corporate entities may be named non-compliant and prosecuted through the Luxembourg courts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Dépôt des comptes annuels) – where the SCSp is subject to publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the partners, and in all cases no later than seven months after the financial year-end; e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal demand to regularize; court fines up to EUR 5,000; failure for six months after formal notice can trigger commercial court strike-off proceedings and general partner liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit is triggered when, for two consecutive financial years, the SCSp exceeds two of the following three thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce 50. Audit is also required if the SCSp is an AIF or managed by an AIFM, if the limited partners contractually require it, or if the partnership agreement so provides.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be elected for statutory accounts where Luxembourg rules permit.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must annually validate its beneficial-owner data in the RBE within one month of the anniversary of the original declaration, irrespective of whether any partnership-interest transfer occurred. Any transfer of limited-partnership or general-partner interests that changes natural-person ultimate ownership must be reported to the RBE within one month of knowledge, and the general partner must update the internal partners' register and, if applicable, the RCS file.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Partner and Management Resolutions
Register of Transfers of Partnership Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500–6,000 per annum depending on the domiciliation and corporate agent provider, volume of secretarial work, and AML/KYC obligations.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–18,000 per audit cycle for a typical SCSp if audit thresholds are met or audit is required by contract; regulated or consolidated structures attract higher fees.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the SCSp level because the SCSp is fully tax-transparent; a Luxembourg taxable operating company is otherwise subject to an aggregate statutory rate of 24.94% (17% corporate income tax + 7% unemployment fund surcharge + municipal business tax at Luxembourg City rate).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is exempt from entity-level Luxembourg CIT; qualifying Luxembourg corporate entities may benefit from the participation exemption, the IP box (80% deduction of qualifying IP income, producing an effective rate of approximately 5.0%), and the notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity. SCSp partners remain subject to tax in their own jurisdiction on their allocable share.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward for Luxembourg taxable entities; no carryback. Annual loss carryforward utilization is capped at 70% of the amount by which taxable income exceeds EUR 100,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No standalone SCSp corporate income tax return is due; the transparent partnership's allocable income is reported on the partners' Luxembourg returns (Form 700 for resident individuals, Form 520 for resident corporate partners) with an attached SCSp allocation schedule. Filing is performed via MyGuichet / the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) e-filing channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Calendar-year returns are due no later than 31 May of the following year; e-filed declarations are generally automatically extended to 31 December where the taxpayer files through MyGuichet. Non-calendar-year partnerships file within the period announced by the tax office, typically by the sixth month after the close of the accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares the partner's allocable share of the SCSp's Luxembourg-source or commercially attributable taxable income for the calendar year, after contractual profit/loss allocation and any preferred return or carried-interest adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner enters the share only to the extent the income is attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment, Luxembourg real estate, or other Luxembourg-source income taxable in Luxembourg. Otherwise the amount is reported in the partner's residence country with a note that the SCSp is fiscally transparent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies each partner by Luxembourg RPE/LU tax number, class of partnership interests, capital contributed, profit-sharing percentage, admission/exit dates, and the detailed allocation of revenue, deductible expenses, and tax credits among partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the audited or agreed SCSp financial statements, the partnership agreement, and, where treaty relief is sought, a tax residency certificate from the partner's jurisdiction of residence. The certificate must evidence that the partner, and not the SCSp, is the taxable owner of the income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Covers Luxembourg withholding taxes suffered, quarterly prepayments, and foreign tax credits passed through from the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim treaty-based reductions or refunds of any Luxembourg source tax only if a valid tax residency certificate and Form 166D or equivalent claim documentation are submitted. The partner may not claim personal allowances or standard deductions on the Luxembourg return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from EUR 50 to EUR 10,000 depending on taxable income and repeated defaults; late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month and a 10% late-payment surcharge applies. Tax evasion through deliberate non-filing may trigger criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% for dividends paid by a Luxembourg taxable company to shareholders. An SCSp is tax-transparent, and profit withdrawals by its partners are not legally classified as dividends; therefore no Luxembourg WHT is imposed on such distributions. A corporate partner may in any case rely on the Luxembourg participation exemption and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive to obtain a 0% rate where it holds at least 10% of the subsidiary's capital for 12 continuous months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) obtain a valid tax residency certificate from the partner's residence jurisdiction; (2) submit a written exemption/refund application to the competent Luxembourg tax office before or at the time of distribution; (3) provide the SCSp partnership agreement and ownership schedule; (4) complete the ACD prescribed withholding-tax exemption form available on MyGuichet; and (5) if the claim is rejected, file an objection within three months of the Luxembourg assessment. Treaty benefits may also require satisfaction of the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no statutory withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments (0% statutory rate). Most Luxembourg tax treaties also grant 0% on interest and royalties, although some older treaties permit up to 10% on royalty payments unless the Principal Purpose Test is met; no WHT applies at the SCSp level because it is transparent.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Luxembourg Local File threshold applies to a pure pass-through SCSp; for a taxable Luxembourg entity performing 3PL functions, the tax administration follows the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and generally expects contemporaneous documentation where related-party cross-border transactions exceed EUR 500,000 per annum, or where the entity is a routine contract logistics provider. Master File and Country-by-Country reporting are mandatory where the ultimate parent group has consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no Economic Substance Regulations statute comparable to offshore regimes, but the ATAD general anti-abuse rule, the MLI Principal Purpose Test, and Luxembourg case-law 'abus de droit' require genuine activity and business purpose. A cross-dock/overseas 3PL with actual employees, warehouse space, inventory management, contractual trade terms, and profit-and-loss accountability demonstrates sufficient substance; an SCSp without any operations or decision-making functions is challengeable and may be denied treaty and participation relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion - intentional under-declaration of SCSp allocable profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting cross-border e-commerce fulfillment revenue, manufacturing fictitious management fee deductions, backdating partner allocations, or understating warehouse inventory to shift taxable profit to low-tax partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the entire taxable income, 10% late-payment surcharge, monthly interest of 0.6%, administrative fines up to EUR 250,000, and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Luxembourg General Tax Law where intent is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or managing partners who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the underpaid tax, civil restitution, and monetary penalties. The corporate veil can be pierced where the SCSp is found to be a sham, leading to personal asset freezing, exit/travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a letterbox conduit with no employees, no warehouse, no operational contracts, no local management, and no commercial rationale, while allocating non-resident partners' income away from Luxembourg or treaty-protected jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of treaty benefits under the MLI Principal Purpose Test, retroactive tax assessments, denial of deduction of intercompany charges, and re-characterisation of the arrangement under the abuse-of-law doctrine; administrative fines and criminal liability may follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A general partner or corporate director may be personally assessed for taxes due when SCSp assets are insufficient, and directors can be held liable for fraudulent misrepresentation, subject to disqualification orders and criminal penalties for falsification of statutory accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the cross-dock fulfillment platform to disguise unexplained bulk cash transfers, conceal beneficial ownership, process payments through shell partners, or ship goods to or from sanctioned jurisdictions while circumventing Luxembourg know-your-customer controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML fines for legal entities reach up to EUR 5 million or 10% of total annual turnover; criminal money-laundering is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to EUR 250,000, increased to 10 years' imprisonment for aggravated offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers and directors can be personally fined, banned from managing Luxembourg entities, and criminally prosecuted. Funds and assets involved are subject to confiscation, and travel restrictions may be imposed during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to document transfer pricing and maintain substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying intercompany fees from the SCSp to related overseas parties without a comparability analysis, functional profile, contractual evidence, or contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, particularly where the Luxembourg entity lacks substance and assumes no entrepreneurial risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward transfer pricing adjustment, recapture of all claimed deductions, gross-up of payments, 10% surcharge, monthly late interest, and administrative fines for deficient records. Where VAT registration is also required and omitted, backdated assessments and VAT penalties apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for at least 5% of unpaid corporate taxes where accounting records are absent, incomplete, or falsified, and for monetary compensation orders in action civile claims; in serious cases, criminal sanctions including imprisonment apply.
